summary: Centralized CalDAV change recording at the EventService transaction boundary: added a caldav_event_changes revision log (migration 0025), recorded exactly one change per committed base create/update/delete, tombstoned the DAV mapping on native delete to keep its FK satisfied, and exposed an ordered change-log read API (list_changes_since) for T11 sync tokens.
defects: MCP internal API (backend/src/mcp_internal.rs) event create/update handlers use raw SQL that does not match the current events schema (non-existent start_utc/end_utc columns, event_kind='default' violates the CHECK constraint, omits NOT NULL created_by_user_id/last_edited_by_user_id) and do not route through EventService, so MCP mutations are not recorded in the CalDAV change log. Pre-existing and outside T10 scope.
follow_up: T11 should build sync-token encoding/decoding on top of CaldavRepository::list_changes_since and resolve each change's resource (ensure_resource for created/updated, tombstone lookup for deleted).
Moves (update with target_calendar_id != source_calendar_id) currently record a single 'updated' change against the target calendar; T12 should emit remove/add pairs.
create_recurring and occurrence mutations are intentionally not recorded; T12/T14 should extend coverage.
important_context: Change recording is centralized in EventService::create/update/delete (base paths only), so browser, DAV, and any future EventService-based mutation record exactly one change per commit and none on rollback; the DAV layer adds no separate recording (no double-count).

EventService::delete now tombstones the live caldav_event_resources mapping (event_id->NULL, deleted_at set) within the same transaction before deleting the event, preventing the mapping's foreign-key violation and leaving a durable tombstone consistent with T09.
caldav_event_changes.id is the monotonically increasing revision; list_changes_since(calendar_id, after_revision, limit) pages it in ascending order.
